What degraded

  • Shipped at the round cap at 6.726, 1.274 under the 8.0 top rung. The craft floor stood down with the art median at 5.8.
  • All three judges ranked the hero hull, a chassis model, as the top art defect in every round. It is queued for the kit as marine-models-built-in-chassis.
  • The aerial frames 4 and 7 read as noise or a game board in every round. A lower camera on frame 4 was tried in round 3, was worse, and was reverted.
  • Frames 2 and 3 carry Saronic's own claims, and every judge called them cuttable. The county half of the story rests on the Texas Tribune, because Cameron County's agendas are scanned PDFs with no text.
  • No frame names a next step for a reader. The record holds no meeting, review date or published agreement to point to.
  • The scanner's daily count and cap were not measured. This session has no D1 access.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it The tax break came first. Saronic's Brownsville shipyard, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

The county decided before Saronic did.

The Texas Tribune reported on June 18th that the Cameron County Commissioners Court approved a $211 million tax break for Saronic. The court hoped the company would pick the Port of Brownsville. Opponents told the court it would take money from public schools.

That month Saronic told the Tribune it had not yet chosen a site.

The Tribune reported a 95% abatement over 20 years. It would require 35% of the full-time workforce to be local. The break would shrink if Saronic fell short of job projections.

On September 30th Saronic broke ground in Brownsville. It calls Port Alpha a software-defined yard for autonomous and manned ships. It puts private capital at more than $3 billion and direct jobs at up to 10,000.

Up to 10,000 is Saronic's own figure. Who will count the jobs, and when?

#CameronCounty #PortOfBrownsville #Saronic

The machine changed itself

    No. 45's hero hull, a slab the judges read as a lighthouse and a barge in all three rounds, is now a kit model with a sheer, a flared bow, a bulwark, a chamfered deckhouse, a lattice mast with radomes and one matte plate. Re-rendering no. 45's frames 2, 3 and 5 against it gave a ship where the slab was
  • For a maintainer: qa reads a dek's glyph halo on flat haze as a rule
    Three decks now (40, 41, 45), each worked around by hand. The fix is in qa.py under .claude, which no run edits (UPGRADE_BACKLOG 2026-10-07 item 2)
  • Carried for a maintainer: engine render artifacts and missing ground contact
    7 runs and 21 rounds, and 7 runs and 20 rounds, still the most named defects the kit can't reach. assets/js/txthree.js is human lane

Every change is logged in ledger/carousel/upgrades.json.

Notes

The record. Re-verification stamped 16 items and wrote 19 dated unconfirmed lines, and tx-2026-0127 gained a claim from the Supreme Court of Texas's October 6th submission schedule. Admitted tx-2026-0204, Saronic's Port Alpha groundbreaking at the Port of Brownsville on a Cameron County abatement. Held nothing new. The deck. Nine rendered frames of the Brownsville Ship Channel at noon. Round 1's integrity judge failed frame 9 for writing a capability ceiling as a length, and round 2 repaired it with the judge's own wording. No hard fail stands. The web edition first rendered '$211 tax break' and '95%%' through its tokens, and every check passed both. The built page caught them, and they are fixed and queued.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
